cabin_co2_mmHg.label: Cabin CO2 (1-hour average)
cabin_co2_mmHg.why: Possible high CO2: the 1-hour average is {delta} {unit} from the nearest limit.
cabin_co2_mmHg.action: Move to open airflow, check fans, re-test in an hour. Tell the flight surgeon if it stays high.
cabin_co2_mmHg.howToMeasure: Read the cabin CO2 sensor and log the 1-hour average partial pressure in mmHg.
cabin_co2_mmHg.whyItMatters: NASA limits the 1-hour average CO2 in the habitable volume to 3 mmHg. Most CO2 symptoms are not confirmed in flight, so treat an alert as a possible cause only.
cabin_co2_mmHg.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-004 (CO2 technical brief) for the 3 mmHg limit; the 2.8 mmHg Watch edge and the Normal, Watch and Act mapping are design values

cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.label: Cabin CO2 (7-day average)
cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.why: Possible slow CO2 build-up: the 7-day average is {delta} {unit} from the 2.5 mmHg line.
cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.action: Check fans and filters, increase airflow, and re-test. Tell the flight surgeon if headaches are logged.
cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.howToMeasure: Log the average of the last 7 days of cabin CO2 in mmHg.
cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.whyItMatters: NASA notes that a 7-day average below 2.5 mmHg keeps headache incidence under 1%.
cabin_co2_7day_avg_mmHg.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-004 (CO2 technical brief) for 2.5 mmHg; band mapping is a design value

symptom_check.label: Symptom check
symptom_check.why: Possible CO2 or cabin-air symptoms are logged (code {delta} from none).
symptom_check.action: Re-test cabin air, move to open airflow, and tell the flight surgeon if symptoms persist.
symptom_check.howToMeasure: Enter 0 if none logged. Enter 1 for headache or vision change on 2 or more days. Enter 2 if it persists after the suggested action, or for nausea with fatigue.
symptom_check.whyItMatters: Headache and vision change can have several causes, including fluid shifts; the log helps the flight surgeon decide.

body_temperature.label: Body temperature
body_temperature.why: Temperature is {delta} {unit} above your usual, more than 2 standard deviations.
body_temperature.action: Re-measure, rest, and tell the flight surgeon if it stays up for 3 days.
body_temperature.howToMeasure: Take your temperature each morning and log it.
body_temperature.whyItMatters: A rise from your own baseline, together with poor sleep, can be an early sign of a possible infection-like problem.

sleep_hours.label: Sleep
sleep_hours.why: Sleep is {delta} {unit} below your usual, more than 2 standard deviations.
sleep_hours.action: Protect a full sleep period tonight and tell the flight surgeon if it stays low for 3 days.
sleep_hours.howToMeasure: Log the hours you slept each morning.
sleep_hours.whyItMatters: Judged against your own baseline, not an 8-hour rule. Short sleep together with a temperature rise can point to a possible infection-like problem.

infection_like.why: Temperature is up and sleep is down for 3 days: a possible infection-like pattern.
infection_like.action: Rest, recheck temperature, and tell the flight surgeon.

infection_like_with_symptoms.why: Temperature up, sleep down and symptoms logged together for 3 days: a possible infection-like problem that needs attention.
